indicatorPicker.buildNew: Build a new one with AI
indicatorPicker.buildSub: Describe an indicator — the AI builds it for your chart

empty.fav: Star (★) an indicator to keep it here.
empty.mine: No AI indicators yet — use Build with AI to make one.

mineAbout.title: What are My indicators?
mineAbout.about: Indicators you built by describing them to the AI. They work on every chart like the built-in ones. Use Edit to change one in plain words, or delete it.

all.title: How do indicators work?
all.about: Every indicator available on this chart. Click a row to add it, click again to remove it. Overlays draw on top of the price; panel indicators get their own space under the chart. Star the ones you use most to find them under Favorites.

fav.title: What are Favorites?
fav.about: Your starred indicators, kept here for quick access. Click the ☆ next to any indicator to add it.

on.title: What's on your chart?
on.about: Everything currently drawn on this chart. Click a row to remove it, or use Clear all.

movingAverages.name: Moving Averages
movingAverages.question: What are moving averages?
movingAverages.about: Smooth out price to show the underlying trend. Price above a rising average leans bullish, below a falling one bearish. Faster averages (EMA 9/20) react quickly to turns; slower ones (100/200) act as long-term support and resistance. Crossovers between a fast and slow average are classic trend-change signals.

trend.name: Trend
trend.question: What do trend indicators show?
trend.about: Tell you which way the market is heading and how strong that move is. Use them to stay with the trend, spot when it's weakening, and place trailing stops — e.g. Parabolic SAR dots flip sides when the trend turns, and Ichimoku's cloud shows trend, momentum and support in one view.

momentum.name: Momentum
momentum.question: What is momentum?
momentum.about: Measure how fast price is moving and whether that push is speeding up or fading. They flag overbought and oversold conditions, and divergences — price making a new high while momentum doesn't — often warn of a reversal before it shows up in price.

oscillators.name: Oscillators
oscillators.question: How do oscillators work?
oscillators.about: Swing between fixed levels or around zero, each in its own panel. Extreme readings point to stretched moves likely to snap back; crossing the zero line confirms a shift in direction. Best in ranging markets, and as confirmation alongside a trend tool.

volatility.name: Volatility
volatility.question: What does volatility tell you?
volatility.about: Show how much price is moving, not which way. Bands and channels widen in wild markets and tighten before big moves (a 'squeeze'). ATR-based tools help size stops and positions so a normal wiggle doesn't knock you out of a trade.

volume.name: Volume
volume.question: Why does volume matter?
volume.about: Look at the money behind each move. Rising price on rising volume is a move with conviction; price rising on falling volume is suspect. VWAP marks the average price paid today — a fair-value line many traders buy and sell around.

levelsZones.name: Levels & Zones
levelsZones.question: What are levels & zones?
levelsZones.about: Draw the prices that matter on the chart: support and resistance, Fibonacci retracements, the day's high and low, and CME gaps. These are where price often reacts — useful for entries, targets and stop placement.

smartMoney.name: Smart Money
smartMoney.question: What is Smart Money?
smartMoney.about: Concepts used to track where large players likely bought or sold: order blocks, fair-value gaps, breaks of structure and retests, plus candlestick patterns and Wyckoff phases. They highlight zones price tends to revisit before continuing.
